Status labels used in this document: VERIFIED (confirmed in the current source code or existing documents) · PROTOTYPE (works in the React/LocalStorage prototype with mock or simulated behaviour) · PROPOSED (recommended production design, not built) · PENDING CONFIRMATION (needs a client decision) · NOT IMPLEMENTED · NOT VERIFIED.

Purpose

Describe the architecture of the current prototype (VERIFIED) and the target production architecture (PROPOSED), their components, boundaries, data flows and integration points.

Scope

Frontend, backend target, database, integrations, deployment, security architecture and scalability strategy.

5. Frontend architecture (VERIFIED)

  • Single navigation configuration (src/config/navigation.js, 206 entries) drives routes, menus, breadcrumbs, search and route permissions.
  • Pages are lazy-loaded; three layouts: AppLayout (office), DriverLayout, CustomerLayout.
  • State: React contexts (AuthContext, ThemeContext, DashboardPeriodContext) + storage subscriptions (useSyncExternalStore over storageService.subscribe, cross-tab storage events).
  • Rule of the codebase: page → hook → service → storageService; pages never touch storage.
  • Details: BM-ARC-002 (Low-Level Design (LLD)).

6. Backend target architecture (PROPOSED)

  • Django 5 project with apps: core, accounts, masterdata, orders, logistics, inventory, documents, billing, comms, analytics, integrations.
  • DRF viewsets with permission classes mapped 1:1 to the 110 permission keys; object-level scope filters per role.
  • Service layer (Python) re-implements the prototype services’ rules; the prototype services are the executable specification (messages and edge cases).
  • Transactions with select_for_update on stock rows and order status changes; idempotency keys for state-changing endpoints (approve, confirm, complete, write-off).
  • Celery for asynchronous work; Channels for WebSockets; drf-spectacular for OpenAPI.

7. Database architecture

Prototype: LocalStorage keys described in BM-DAT-001 (Current Prototype Data Model (LocalStorage)). Production: PostgreSQL schema with ≈45 tables, audit columns, soft delete, indexes and constraints — BM-DAT-002 (Proposed Production Database Design).

8. Integration architecture

Every adapter is behind an interface with a sandbox / mock implementation (as in the prototype) so that tests never call live providers. Contract details: BM-API-019 (Integration Specification (External Systems)).

9. Deployment architecture — PROPOSED

Containers (API, Channels, workers, beat, Nginx) on a managed container platform or VMs; managed PostgreSQL and Redis; object storage; CDN for the web app; separate test, staging and production environments. See BM-INF-003 (Infrastructure, Network Architecture and Server Specification) and BM-INF-006 (Docker Architecture and Deployment Guide).

10. Security architecture

TLS everywhere; JWT access (15 min) + refresh tokens; Argon2id; MFA for privileged roles; server-side RBAC and object scope; OTP hashing and rate limiting; signed URLs for files; audit log; secrets in a vault; WAF and rate limits. Prototype controls are simulated. See BM-SEC-002 (Security Architecture).

11. Data flow — order to delivery (production)

12. Component responsibilities and system boundaries

  • Inside the system: all workflows from order capture to delivery note, master data, rules, notifications, reporting, (optionally) invoices and inventory.
  • Outside the system: ERP accounting and invoicing (unless confirmed), payment collection, map and messaging infrastructure, SAP master data ownership (stage 2), vehicle hardware.

13. External dependencies

Google Maps Platform / Routes API · SMS / WhatsApp provider · email provider · OCR engine · SAP · app stores · hosting provider. All PENDING CONFIRMATION of account and contract.

14. Scalability strategy — PROPOSED

Stateless API containers scaled horizontally behind the load balancer; Channels scaled with a Redis channel layer; Celery queues separated (messaging, ocr, reports); PostgreSQL vertical scaling + read replica for reports; GPS points written in batches and partitioned by month (or PostGIS / TimescaleDB if volumes require); CDN for static assets. Capacity numbers depend on confirmed volumes (NFR-SCAL-002).
